 Judgment

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-III, Vijayapura (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.582/2018, vide its judgment and award dated 20.08.2019.
2.
The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 14.02.2018 when a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28/EN-9225 ridden in a rash and negligent manner dashed the claimant.
As a result, he suffered injuries and was admitted in the hospital for NC: 2023:KHC-K:5512 treatment.
The claimant claimed that he was a business man and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
He claimed that due to the injuries suffered in the accident, he was out of business and was thus deprived of ability to earn any income.
He therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.
3. The owner denied the accident and contents of the claim petition.
The insurer also denied the accident as well as injuries suffered by the claimant.
It claimed that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid licence and hence, there was violation of the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P10.
He also examined a doctor as PW.2 who deposed that the claimant had suffered fracture of distal end of right radius and NC: 2023:KHC-K:5512 fracture of proximal tibia joint union.

He deposed that the claimant had suffered 20% to 25%
disability to right upper limb and 10% to 15% to the right lower limb.

sentences.text: Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle and that in the said accident, the claimant suffered injuries.

The Tribunal considered the age of the claimant as 47 years and his notional income at Rs.8,000/-
per month.
It also held that the x-ray of right wrist showed malunited fracture at the distal end of radius and fracture of proximal tibia joint.
The Tribunal however noticed the evidence of PW.2 who deposed that the claimant did not avail any follow up treatment resulting in malunion of fracture of radius.

Therefore, the Tribunal held that the fracture of malunion was due to negligence on the part of the claimant himself and hence, did not award any compensation towards loss NC:
2023:KHC-K:5512 of income due to disability.

The Tribunal considering the above, awarded the following compensation:
Medical expenses Rs.60,000/-
Pain and suffering Rs.30,000/-
Loss of amenities Rs.15,000/-
Loss of income during bed Rs.10,000/-
ridden period Attendant charges Rs.5,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer to pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the claimant is in appeal.
7. The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the accident involving the motorcycle as well as the injuries caused to the claimant is not in dispute.
He submitted that the wound certificate at Ex.P4 indicated swelling on the right wrist and fracture of distal end of radius and proximal right tibia.
He contended that the claimant was admitted on 14.02.2018 and discharged on 29.02.2018.
He therefore submitted that malunion NC: 2023:KHC-K:5512 fracture of radius was due to the accident and not due to negligence on the part of the claimant.

He submitted that the claimant being a business man, the fractures had caused disability which must have been assessed in the light of the evidence of PW.2 that the claimant had difficulty in movement of right knee joint and that he was difficulty in walking.
He therefore submitted that the compensation be enhanced.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that there was no proof of disability and the fracture of tibial joint was united while the malunion fracture of radius was due to the negligence on the part of the claimant himself.
She therefore contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as learned counsel for the insurer.

3 10.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimant, the claimant suffered injuries in the accident involving the motorcycle.

The evidence on record discloses that fracture of distal end of radius was malunited which meant that the movement of the right wrist was restricted and it was a permanent disability that could not have been glossed over by the Tribunal.
Further more, the claimant had suffered fracture of proximal tibial joint which too must have affected his ability to move around.

In that view of the mater, this Court considers it appropriate to assess the disability at 12% to the whole body having regard to the evidence that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 20% to 25% to the right lower limb and 10% to 15% left lower limb.
In additional, notional income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.11,750/-.

Consequently, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation, which is as follows:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5512 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-
Attendant charges, Rs.10,000/-
conveyance charges and nourished food Medical expenses Rs.60,000/-
Loss of income during laid Rs.35,250/-
up period Loss of income due to Rs.2,19,960/-
disability Loss of amenities Rs.20,000/-
Total Rs.3,85,210/-
11.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.3,85,210/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.2,65,210/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
